{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Commerce One hosting and licence agreement

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Twelve clauses are compliant (several at the fallback rather than the preferred position), five are deviations requiring redlines, and one expected clause is missing entirely.

The commercial core is favourable to us. Commerce One's IP infringement indemnity covers us **and our Customers**, sits entirely outside the Section 9 cap (better than our fallback super-cap) and is non-reciprocal. The licence grant is perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable to our Customers and survives termination. There is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, no MFN, no liquidated damages and no non-solicit binding us. The audit right meets our preferred position, and renewal terms (12 months, 30-day window, fixed Year 2–5 pricing) do likewise.

Three items drive the negotiation. First, **Section 13.5 vests our own interface code and hosting Developments in Commerce One** wherever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back — an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor and, under our playbook, walk-away territory. Second, the **Section 9 cap** is narrowed to amounts paid for the single transaction to which the liability relates and carves out only Section 8, leaving confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud inside a materially sub-12-month cap; that fails our fallback. Third, for a hosted service there is **no transition assistance and no data-return or deletion obligation** on expiry or termination. Two further deviations — the absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right across a five-year term, and a 60-day warranty running from the Effective Date rather than acceptance — are straightforward to fix. Vendor insurance is absent altogether despite Commerce One hosting the transacting environment and supplying on-site personnel.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Shared Resources (13.5) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 9 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 Indemnification |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 Term and Termination |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 14 Miscellaneous |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2/3 Grant of Rights |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 17 Payment Terms |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 2/3 Grant of Rights |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 1 Definitions |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11 Term and Termination (11.3) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 7 Warranties and Disclaimer |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 4 Fees |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14 Miscellaneous |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | Exhibit B — Pricing |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Exhibit B — Revenue Sharing Fees |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 13 Shared Resources |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 11 Term and Termination |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 Miscellaneous |

---

## Walk-away items

1. **Vendor ownership of our Developments (§ 13.5).** The "unless supported" reversal assigns Developments we create — including our own interface code and hosting Developments — to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back. This is walk-away territory under the IP rule and must be deleted. Commerce One retains its pre-existing materials and the Software itself under Section 2.8, which we accept. We also flag that ownership of enhancements to the Software developed by us is left to future negotiation and should be resolved now.

No other finding reaches walk-away territory. In particular, California law with AAA arbitration in San Francisco County sits within our accepted fallback; walk-away is reserved for an unlisted home jurisdiction or a foreign seat.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue redlines on the five deviations:**
   - *§ 13.5* — delete the clause vesting Corio-created Developments in Commerce One where Commerce One supports them, so Developments created by us stay ours.
   - *§ 9* — restore a true 12-month fee cap (removing the "transaction which the liability relates to" narrowing) and add an Excluded Claims sentence covering indemnification, confidentiality (§ 10), gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud. The mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages is acceptable as drafted.
   - *§ 11* — add a Corio termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. No deletion is needed on the Vendor side, as Commerce One likewise has no convenience exit.
   - *§ 11.3* — insert a fallback-level transition assistance and data-return paragraph, including return or export of our and our Customers' data held in the MarketSite.net Service and deletion certification.
   - *§ 7* — extend the conformance warranty to 90 days from acceptance and remove the fixed calendar cut-off (acceptance testing itself runs to 31 December 1999, so the current 60-day Effective Date period can lapse at or before acceptance). Remedies and the no-malicious-code and IP warranties are otherwise adequate.
2. **Insert a short insurance covenant** in Miscellaneous at the fallback level (CGL, E&O and cyber cover, certificates on request), given Commerce One hosts the environment through which our Customers transact and supplies on-site personnel.
3. **Confirm we are not seeking changes** to the compliant items, including those sitting at the fallback, and record the noted-only points for the file: the § 14 assignment consent standard is not expressed as "not to be unreasonably withheld" and the direct-competitor exception could require consent on an acquisition by a Commerce One competitor; Affiliates are not named in the licence grant and the Territory is limited to North America (with the § 2.10 expansion mechanism); the audit notice period is "reasonable notice" rather than a fixed period; there is no Vendor renewal reminder or express CPI/3% uplift cap; and we prefer courts to mandatory arbitration.
4. **Escalate § 13.5 to the business** ahead of the next negotiation session, flagging it as the one item on which we are prepared to walk away, and settle our position on ownership of Software enhancements we develop."}
